autor: Michael of Cesena (c. 1270–1342), minister general of the Friars Minor 1316–1328, in a notarial instrument drawn up in the Franciscan convent of Avignon
quelle: Stephani Baluzii Tutelensis Miscellanea novo ordine digesta, ed. Joannes Dominicus Mansi, tom. III (Lucca: apud Vincentium Junctinium, sumptibus Joannis Riccomini, 1762), pp. 238–239. Internet Archive, bub_gb_rPboqzeWk5QC (Google scan). Public domain.
hinweis: Mansi printed the appeal from a manuscript copy that still contains the copyist's instruction to insert the Perugia letter ('see above on folio …'). The machine reading of the two-column long-s type is unusable; the Latin was transcribed from the page images, with the long s set as s and the quotation marks at the head of every line dropped. The appeal is carried almost in full; the cuts are marked […]. The longer appeal Michael issued at Pisa in 1328 follows in the same volume (pp. 246 ff.) and is not carried. The English is this site's working translation (CC0).

sections.blurb: Michael of Cesena's secret appeal, drawn up by a notary in the Franciscan convent of Avignon four days after the pope called him 'a supporter of heretics': the summons, the illness, the four quiet months, the audience of 9 April, Perugia signed again, the argument that a pope who condemns Exiit condemns himself, and the appeal made 'from a just fear'.

units.orig: In Nomine Domini Amen. Anno a Nativitate Domini millesimo tercentesimo vigesimo octavo, Indictione undecima, Die XIII. mensis Aprilis in Civitate Avinionensi in Domo Fratrum minorum coram infrascriptis religiosis, & honestis personis, & me infrascripto notario, ibi Reverendus in Christo Pater Frater Michael de Cesena Ordinis Fratrum minorum Generalis Minister & in sacra pagina Doctor dixit, & protestatus fuit, provocavit, appellavit, & fecit, prout inferius continetur. Ego Frater Michael de Cesena Ordinis Fratrum minorum Minister generalis, & servus, meo proprio nomine, & etiam nomine, & vice Capituli Generalis, ac totius Ordinis Fratrum minorum, & singulorum fratrum ipsius Ordinis, ac omnium mihi adhaerentium, & adhaerere volentium, dico, propono, & protestor coram vobis religiosis, & honestis viris, quod Dominus Joannes, qui se Joannem Papam XXII. appellat, vocavit me ad suam praesentiam per quasdam litteras sub Bulla sua, quarum tenor talis est. Joannes Episcopus servus servorum Dei. Dilecto filio Michaeli generali ministro Ordinis Fratrum minorum salutem, & apostolicam benedictionem. Cum propter aliqua negocia tuum ordinem contingentia tua sit opportuna praesentia, tibi in virtute obedientiae praecipiendo mandamus, quod infra mensem a praesentatione praesentium computandum te studeas nostro conspectui praesentare personaliter. Datum Avinionis VI. Idus Junii Pontificatus nostri anno XI.
units.en: In the name of the Lord, amen. In the year from the Nativity of the Lord 1328, eleventh indiction, on the thirteenth day of the month of April, in the city of Avignon, in the house of the Friars Minor, before the religious and honest persons written below and me, the notary written below, the reverend father in Christ brother Michael of Cesena, general minister of the order of Friars Minor and doctor of the sacred page, said, protested, provoked, appealed and did as is contained below. I, brother Michael of Cesena, general minister and servant of the order of Friars Minor, in my own name and also in the name and on behalf of the general chapter and of the whole order of Friars Minor and of each friar of that order, and of all who adhere or wish to adhere to me, say, set forth and protest before you, religious and honest men, that the lord John, who calls himself Pope John XXII, summoned me to his presence by letters under his bull, whose tenor is this: John, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Michael, general minister of the order of Friars Minor, greeting and apostolic blessing. Since your presence is needed for some business touching your order, we command you in virtue of obedience to take care to present yourself in person before us within a month of the presentation of these letters. Given at Avignon on the sixth day before the Ides of June, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.
units.note: The summons is dated 8 June 1327. Mansi prints before the instrument an introduction (cut here) explaining that Michael, 'seeing that the lord John meant to force him to abjure the determination of the general chapter', appealed on 13 April 1328. 'Who calls himself Pope John XXII': from the first line the appeal no longer grants him the title. The notary is the Franciscan Guido de Pupio, named in the Pisa version.

units.orig: Quibus Litteris receptis cum essem corporali infirmitate gravatus me excusavi ratione dictae infirmitatis, & ipsam excusationem eidem Domino Joanni transmisi, & de ea sibi fidem feci per literas & testimonia vicarii Domini Episcopi Irtanensis, & plurium aliorum fide dignorum, & etiam per litteras Illustrissimi Principis, & Domini Domini Roberti Dei gratia Hierusalem, & Siciliae Regis, qui de ipsa mea infirmitate certificatus fuerat per medicum suum, quem ad me visitandum in dicta infirmitate transmiserat. Qua excusatione rationabili intellecta per ipsum Dominum Joannem ipse mihi mandavit, & mandari & insinuari fecit, quod habebat me rationabiliter excusatum, & quod non fuerat suae intentionis, nec volebat quod supra posse laborarem in veniendo ad eum, sed cum commode possem ad eum assumpta corporis sanitate venirem. Postea ego corporali sanitate aliqualiter assumpta studui pro posse ad ipsius Domini Joannis praesentiam festinare: Et cum multis periculis propriae personae 2. die mensis Decembris Anno Domini millesimo tercentesimo vigesimo septimo ad ipsum veni, & me coram eo personaliter praesentavi, & ipse me pacifice, ac benigne recepit, audivit, & pertractavit, & postea expressit, & specificavit mihi causam, quare me vocaverat ad suam praesentiam, dicens, quod me vocaverat ex eo, quod ipse intellexerat, quod aliquae provinciae dicti ordinis propter malum regimen ipsarum provinciarum ministrorum, detrimenta, & pericula gravia patiebantur: quod quoque ipse mihi hoc non imputabat, nec imputandum esse censebat pro eo quod ego per me non habebam potestatem providendi provinciis de ministris: & specialiter ipse Dominus Joannes tunc mihi nominavit Provincias Sancti Francisci, & Aragoniae, in quibus hujusmodi pericula & detrimenta esse dicebat, & mandavit ac commisit mihi, quod ministros dictarum duarum provinciarum absolverem, & eisdem de ministris idoneis, & sufficientibus providerem. Et sic pacifice & quiete de ipsius Domini Joannis voluntate remansi in Avinione a dicta die 2. mensis Decembris usque ad diem VIII. mensis Aprilis, ita quod de nullo crimine vel defectu in dictum tempus me redarguit, nec dixit, nec apparuit, quod sibi forem de aliquo crimine denunciatus, vel etiam accusatus.
units.en: When I received these letters I was burdened with bodily illness, and I excused myself on account of that illness and sent the excuse to the lord John, and gave him proof of it by letters and testimony of the vicar of the lord bishop 'Irtanensis' (so printed) and of many other trustworthy persons, and also by letters of the most illustrious prince and lord, lord Robert, by the grace of God king of Jerusalem and Sicily, who had been assured of my illness by his physician, whom he had sent to visit me in it. The lord John, having understood this reasonable excuse, commanded me, and had it commanded and made known to me, that he held me reasonably excused, and that it had not been his intention, nor did he wish, that I should labour beyond my strength in coming to him, but that I should come to him when I conveniently could, once I had recovered my bodily health. Afterwards, having recovered my health somewhat, I made haste as best I could to the presence of the lord John; and with many dangers to my own person I came to him on the second day of the month of December in the year of the Lord 1327, and presented myself before him in person; and he received me peacefully and kindly, heard me and dealt with me, and afterwards set out and specified to me the reason why he had summoned me to his presence, saying that he had summoned me because he had understood that some provinces of the order were suffering harm and grave dangers through the bad government of their ministers; and that he did not impute this to me, nor thought it should be imputed, since I did not by myself have the power to provide the provinces with ministers; and in particular the lord John then named to me the provinces of Saint Francis and of Aragon, in which he said such dangers and harms existed, and commanded and charged me to remove the ministers of those two provinces and provide them with fit and sufficient ministers. And so I remained at Avignon peacefully and quietly by the will of the lord John from the second day of December to the eighth day of April, so that during that time he did not reproach me with any crime or fault, nor said, nor did it appear, that I had been denounced to him or even accused of any crime.
units.note: Robert of Anjou, king of Naples ('Jerusalem and Sicily'), a protector of the Franciscans, whose physician visited Michael. The province of Saint Francis is Umbria; its minister, Peter de Prato, was present at the audience of 9 April. The appeal builds its legal case carefully: four months without any charge, then a sudden accusation.

units.orig: Et postea ipse Dominus Joannes vocavit me ad suam praesentiam die IX. ipsius mensis Aprilis; & cum fui in ejus praesentia constitutus, & essent ibi praesentes Dominus Frater Bertrandus de Turre Cardinalis, & Fratres Raymundus de Lados Procurator generalis dicti Ordinis, Petrus de Prato minister Provinciae Sancti Francisci, & Laurentius de Malchono Bacalarius Conventus Avinionensis Ordinis praedicti; ipse Dominus Joannes in praedictorum praesentia dixit, & asseruit me fautorem haereticorum, & specialiter increpavit me de quadam littera Capituli generalis facta Perusii, cujus tenor inferius continetur: increpans me, & ipsum Capitulum generale, quod pendente quaestione in Curia per ipsum proposita, praesumpseram una cum Capitulo generali eam determinare: quam Literam Capituli generalis frequenter dixit fuisse & esse haereticam, sicut de hujusmodi increpatione & assertione, sive dicto constat etiam per literas manu propria dicti Procuratoris scriptas, & subscriptionibus, ac testimoniis dictorum fratrum roboratas. Et cum eidem Domino Joanni dicerem constanter, quod dicta littera dicti generalis Capituli non erat haeretica, sed Catholica: cum certum sit, quod assertio ipsius generalis Capituli in ipsa littera contenta in sententia eadem est penitus cum determinatione Domini Nicolai Papae III. posita in Decretali Extra de verbor. signif. C. Exiit §. porro. Unde si esset haeretica, sequeretur quod ipse Dominus Nicolaus Papa, qui talem determinationem fecit, fuisset haereticus. Tunc ipse Dominus Joannes praecepit mihi sub poena excommunicationis, privationis officii mei, & inhabilitationis ad quodcumque officium, & beneficium quod non exirem de Romana Curia sine sua licentia.
units.en: And afterwards the lord John summoned me to his presence on the ninth day of that month of April; and when I stood in his presence, and there were present the lord brother Bertrand de la Tour, cardinal, and brothers Raymond de Lados, procurator general of the order, Peter de Prato, minister of the province of Saint Francis, and Laurence de Malchono, bachelor of the convent of Avignon of the said order, the lord John, in their presence, said and asserted that I was a supporter of heretics, and in particular rebuked me for a certain letter of the general chapter made at Perugia, whose tenor is contained below; rebuking me and the general chapter that, while the question he had put was pending in the curia, I had presumed together with the general chapter to determine it; which letter of the general chapter he often said was and is heretical, as is also established concerning this rebuke and assertion, or saying, by letters written by the said procurator's own hand and strengthened by the signatures and testimony of the said brothers. And when I said firmly to the lord John that the letter of the general chapter was not heretical but catholic, since it is certain that the assertion of the general chapter contained in that letter is in its sense entirely the same as the determination of the lord Pope Nicholas III set out in the decretal Exiit, § Porro, under the title On the meaning of words, so that if it were heretical it would follow that the lord Pope Nicholas, who made that determination, had been a heretic: then the lord John commanded me, under pain of excommunication, of deprivation of my office and of disqualification from any office and benefice, not to leave the Roman curia without his permission.
units.note: The scene the game's second half turns on. The Perugia letter is Chron. Perugia [1]–[2]; Exiit § Porro is Exiit [2]. Michael's argument in one sentence: if Perugia is heretical, so was Nicholas III. The order not to leave the curia is what the flight of 26 May broke (Chron. Flight [1]).

units.titel: 'I judge it true': Perugia signed again
units.orig: Tenor autem literae dicti capituli Generalis, quam ipse Dominus Joannes frequenter dixit fuisse haereticam talis est. Universis Christi fidelibus &c. Vide supra in folio . . . . & eam hic pone. Ego frater Michael ordinis fratrum minorum generalis minister, & in sacra pagina magister praedictis consentio, & eam esse veram judico. In cujus rei testimonium sigillum mei officii praesentibus literis appendi jussi, & manu mea propria me subscripsi. Similes subscriptiones, & sigillationes fecerunt magistri, & Bacallarii, & quatuor Provinciales Ministri superius in dicta littera nominati. Haec verba dictae literae dicti capituli generalis & subscriptionum praedictorum ministrorum, magistrorum, & Bacallariorum in sacra pagina. In qua litera, & contentis in ea alii magistri, & Bacallarii dicti ordinis, qui non fuerunt in dicto capitulo generali praesentes, tam de Parisiis, quam de Anglia numero XLI. concordaverunt, & suum super hoc consilium ejusdem sententiae cum praedicta litera capituli generalis dederunt, sicut patet per literas ipsorum magistrorum, & bacallariorum subscriptionibus, & sigillis roboratas. Ex quibus manifeste patet, quod ego cum dicto capitulo, & capitulum una mecum non determinavimus aliquam quaestionem dubiam, nec aliquid quod possit rationabiliter esse dubium: sed quod per sanctam Ecclesiam Catholicam clare, & expresse determinatum erat, ac diffinitum fideliter confessi fuimus, diximus, & asseruimus, & ad communem omnium fidelium notitiam deducere per dictam literam voluimus, sicut etiam ex nostrae regulae professione facere tenebamur. In cujus principio dicitur, quod volentes hanc vitam accipere, debent credere, & fideliter confiteri, & usque in finem firmiter observare fidem catholicam. Et in fine ipsius regulae de professoribus ejusdem respondetur, ut semper sint subditi, & subjecti pedibus ejusdem sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae, stabiles in fide catholica, paupertatem, humilitatem, & sanctum Evangelium Domini nostri Jesu Christi quod promisimus firmiter observemus. Unde sequitur quod dictus Dominus Joannes me, & dictum capitulum de determinatione quaestionis in curia pendentis nimis injuste, & irrationabiliter increpavit.
units.en: The tenor of the letter of the said general chapter, which the lord John often said was heretical, is this: 'To all the faithful of Christ', etc. See above on folio …, and put it here. 'I, brother Michael, general minister of the order of Friars Minor and master of the sacred page, consent to the foregoing and judge it true. In witness of which I have ordered the seal of my office to be hung on the present letters, and have signed with my own hand.' The masters and bachelors and the four provincial ministers named above in the letter made similar signatures and sealings. These are the words of the letter of the general chapter and of the signatures of the said ministers, masters and bachelors of the sacred page. With this letter and its contents other masters and bachelors of the order who were not present at the general chapter, both of Paris and of England, forty-one in number, agreed, and gave their counsel of the same judgement as the letter of the general chapter, as appears from the letters of those masters and bachelors, strengthened with their signatures and seals. From which it plainly appears that I with the chapter, and the chapter with me, did not determine any doubtful question, nor anything that could reasonably be doubtful, but faithfully confessed, said and asserted what had been clearly and expressly determined and defined by the holy catholic Church, and wished by that letter to bring it to the common knowledge of all the faithful, as we were bound to do by the profession of our rule; at whose beginning it is said that those who wish to take up this life must believe and faithfully confess the catholic faith and keep it firmly to the end; and at whose end it is answered of its professors that they should always be subject and submissive at the feet of the holy Roman Church, stable in the catholic faith, and firmly keep the poverty, humility and holy Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ which we have promised. From which it follows that the lord John rebuked me and the chapter most unjustly and unreasonably for the determination of the question pending in the curia.
units.note: 'See above on folio … and put it here': the notary's (or the copyist's) instruction to insert the Perugia letter, printed as it stands in the manuscript. The rule of 1223 does begin with 'the catholic faith' and end with subjection 'at the feet of the holy Roman Church': Michael turns the rule's obedience to the Roman Church into an argument against the pope.

units.orig: Attendens igitur quod ipse dominus Joannes per dictam suam assertionem, qua dixit frequenter dictam literam capituli generalis fuisse haereticam, me, & totum ordinem, capitulum generale, & omnes professores, & observatores dictae regulae, quae fundata est in dicta veritate per universalem Ecclesiam determinata, & diffinita de haeresi, & doctrina haeretica redarguit: nobiscum crimen haeresis imposuit, & imponit: Et quod licet diceretur ipsum dominum Joannem jam dudum ante praedictam assertionem, & increpationem tria statuta fecisse, & per mundum publice divulgasse: Quorum primum, incipit, ad conditorem; secundum, cum inter nonnullos; tertium quia quorundam, per quae dictam determinationem Ecclesiae, & confessionem capituli generalis judicasse haereticas videbatur. Tamen mihi nondum pro certo innotuere, quod ipse dominus Joannes firmiter crederet, assereret, & teneret ipsas Ecclesiae determinationem, & dictam literam generalis capituli fore haereticas, sed per dictam suam assertionem & increpationem pro certo innotuit. Insuper attendens, quod ipse Dominus Joannes dictam determinationem in dicta decretali Exiit contentam dicendo haereticam, se ipsum proprio judicio de haeresi judicat & condemnat, prout ex pluribus gestis approbatis, & statutis, ac ordinatis per ipsum ostenditur evidenter. Et primo ex eo quod manifestum fuit tempore generalis concilii Lugdunensis, Viennensis, quod Dominus Clemens quintus sacro approbante concilio fecit declarationem, & decretalem solemnem, quae incipit, Exivi de Paradiso, quam ipse dominus Joannes postmodum approbavit, & eam in septimo libro poni, & inseri fecit, ac mandavit, quod omnes ipsa decretali utantur, tam in judiciis, quam in scholis, ut patet in prooemio, quod ipse dominus Joannes super ipsum librum septimum ordinavit. In qua declaratione Domini Clementis Quinti inter caetera determinatio facta per Dominum Nicolaum III. & posita in dicta Decretali Exiit approbatur, & nominatim abdicatio proprietatis, & dominii omnium rerum tam in speciali quam in communi, quam fratres dicti ordinis profitentur, tanquam caelestis vitae forma, & salutaris doctrina, & tanquam paupertas altissima ad perfectionem deducens, & solo Deo contenta approbatur, & multipliciter commendatur. Ex quibus sequitur manifeste, quod si ipse Dominus Joannes illud, quod tam solemniter approbavit, nunc haereticum asserit, se ipsum de haeresi proprio judicio judicat, & condemnat. […] Sequeretur etiam ex hoc: ex quo Dominus Nicolaus Tertius fecit dictam determinationem fuisset haereticus manifestus, & quod gesta per eum fuissent nulla, & nullius valoris, & momenti, & quod Domini Bonifacius Octavus, & Clemens Quintus ex quo talem determinationem approbaverunt fuissent haeretici, & quod gesta per eos non tenuissent: Et quod Cardinales facti per ipsos Summos Pontifices, & qui consenserunt in ipsam determinationem, non fuissent veri, nec legitimi Cardinales, & quod ipse Dominus Joannes electus ab ipsis nunquam fuisset verus Papa.
units.en: Considering, then, that the lord John, by his assertion, in which he often said that the letter of the general chapter was heretical, convicted me and the whole order, the general chapter, and all the professors and observers of the rule, which is founded on that truth determined and defined by the universal Church, of heresy and heretical doctrine, and laid and lays the crime of heresy on us; and that, although the lord John was said long before this assertion and rebuke to have made three statutes and published them throughout the world, the first beginning Ad conditorem, the second Cum inter nonnullos, the third Quia quorundam, by which he seemed to have judged the determination of the Church and the confession of the general chapter heretical, it had not yet become certainly known to me that the lord John firmly believed, asserted and held that determination of the Church and the letter of the general chapter to be heretical, but by his assertion and rebuke it became certainly known. Considering moreover that the lord John, by calling heretical the determination contained in the decretal Exiit, judges and condemns himself of heresy by his own judgement, as is plainly shown by many acts approved, decreed and ordained by him. First, because it was manifest at the time of the general council of Vienne that the lord Clement V, with the approval of the holy council, made the declaration and solemn decretal beginning Exivi de paradiso, which the lord John afterwards approved and had put and inserted in the seventh book, and commanded that all should use that decretal in courts and in schools, as appears in the preface the lord John set over that seventh book. In which declaration of the lord Clement V, among other things, the determination made by the lord Nicholas III and set out in the decretal Exiit is approved, and by name the renunciation of property and ownership of all things, both individually and in common, which the friars of the order profess, is approved and commended in many ways as the form of heavenly life and saving doctrine, and as the highest poverty leading to perfection and content with God alone. From which it plainly follows that if the lord John now asserts to be heretical what he so solemnly approved, he judges and condemns himself of heresy by his own judgement. […] It would also follow from this that, since the lord Nicholas III made that determination, he would have been a manifest heretic, and his acts null and of no value or force; and that the lords Boniface VIII and Clement V, since they approved that determination, would have been heretics, and their acts would not have held; and that the cardinals made by those supreme pontiffs, and who consented to that determination, would not have been true or lawful cardinals; and that the lord John, elected by them, would never have been true pope.
units.note: The argument in its sharpest form. Michael claims not to have been sure, until 9 April, that the pope really held what his three decretals seemed to say: a legal fiction that let him say he had obeyed until then. The cut adds two more of the pope's own acts: his praise of his predecessors' declarations in Quorundam exigit (Decr. Exigit [1]), and the opening of Gloriosam ecclesiam (1318), the bull against the rebel Spirituals, which praises the order 'from its foundation' as joined to the life and doctrine of Christ. The last sentence is the reductio the whole Franciscan position rests on: if Exiit was heresy, the cardinals who elected John XXII were no cardinals, and he no pope. 'The seventh book' is the Clementines, the collection of Clement V's decretals that John XXII promulgated in 1317.

units.titel: 'A fear that can fall on a steadfast man'
units.orig: Quam ob rem ego praefatus Frater Michael dicti ordinis fratrum minorum generalis minister, sentiens me gravatum, & dictum generale capitulum, & omnes, & singulos fratres dicti ordinis, & ipsum totum ordinem, ac etiam universalem Ecclesiam ex praedictis increpatione, & assertione, ac praecepto factis per ipsum D. Joannem, & ex omnibus aliis gestis, statutis, & ordinatis per ipsum D. Joannem in diminutionem sive derogationem, aut praejudicium, vel infamiam praedictarum confessionum & declarationum saepedicti capituli generalis, & declarationum Dominorum Nicolai III. & Clementis V. & cujuscumque, seu alicujus earum enormiter aggravatum: Et ex probabilibus, & verisimilibus conjecturis, & rationabilibus causis, timens inposterum per ipsum Dominum Joannem fortius aggravari, protestor coram religiosis vobis, & honestis personis, quod ego praefatus Michael justo metu ductus, tali videlicet, qui possit cadere in constantem virum non sum ausus hanc appellationem, & provocationem coram ipso Domino Joanne facere, sive interponere, nec eam sibi porrigere, & praesentare; Unde nunc coram vobis religiosis, & honestis viris personaliter constitutus de isto metu justo protestor, & in vestra praesentia praedictas increpationem, assertionem, & attestationem, ac dictum praeceptum factum per Dominum Joannem, & omnia alia gesta, & facta per ipsum in mei, ac dicti capituli, ac ordinis, & fratrum praejudicium, injuriam, & gravamen, & in derogationem dictarum declarationum Dominorum Nicolai III. & Clementis Quinti, & quodlibet eorum, & omnia, & singula quae sequerentur ex praedictis, vel eorum occasione fierent, fuisse, & esse, & censeri debere nulla, nullius valoris, & momenti; Et quatenus de facto processerunt, sive facta, & gesta sunt, ab eis omnibus, & singulis quae sequuta fuissent, vel sequerentur ex ipsis, in his scriptis dicto nomine coram vobis ad Sedem apostolicam provoco, & appello: Et si & in quantum jura postulant, & requirunt, apostolos instanter, & iterum cum instantia peto […].
units.en: Wherefore I, the said brother Michael, general minister of the order of Friars Minor, feeling myself burdened, and the general chapter, and each and every friar of the order, and the whole order itself, and also the universal Church, enormously burdened by the rebuke, assertion and command made by the lord John, and by all the other acts, statutes and ordinances of the lord John to the diminution, derogation, prejudice or disgrace of the confessions and declarations of the general chapter and of the declarations of the lords Nicholas III and Clement V, or of any of them; and fearing, from probable and likely conjectures and reasonable causes, to be burdened still more heavily by the lord John in future: I protest before you, religious and honest persons, that I, the said Michael, moved by a just fear, namely such a one as can fall on a steadfast man, have not dared to make or lodge this appeal and provocation before the lord John himself, nor to hand it or present it to him. Therefore now, standing in person before you, religious and honest men, I protest this just fear; and in your presence I protest that the said rebuke, assertion and attestation, and the command given by the lord John, and all other acts and deeds by him to the prejudice, injury and burden of me, of the chapter, of the order and of the friars, and to the derogation of the declarations of the lords Nicholas III and Clement V, and each of them, and each and all things that would follow from them or be done on their occasion, were, are and must be held null, of no value or force; and in so far as they have in fact gone forward, or been done and performed, I provoke and appeal in these writings, in the said name, before you, from all and each of them and of what followed or would follow from them, to the apostolic see; and if and in so far as the law demands and requires, I ask urgently, and again urgently, for apostoli […].
units.note: 'A fear that can fall on a steadfast man' (metus qui cadit in constantem virum) is the Roman-law formula for duress that excuses: Michael's reason for appealing in secret, in the Franciscan convent, and not to the pope's face. 'Apostoli' are the letters of dismissal an appellant asks from the judge appealed against. Six weeks later he fled; at Pisa, on 18 September and 12 December 1328, he renewed the appeal 'to the holy catholic Church and to a general council', no longer to the apostolic see.
